---
title: "Posterior summaries in a grade report"
subtitle: "2.13 · after Kline, Rose and Walters (2024), Section VI and slides 61–63 and 69"
description: "Marginal intervals and mean pairwise errors between ordered grades."
---

Each row plots a unit's posterior mean and marginal interval in its grade's color. Cross-grade pairs state a direction; same-grade pairs are withheld; below-diagonal cells average cross-grade error probabilities.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Six sites.** The card states 12 of 15 pairs (share .800), with risk .0417 and expected share wrong .00206. Adjacent-grade cells show .0024 and .0038; the diagonal marks withheld pairs.
- **Reveal by grade.** Only Grade 1 is drawn first, and the matrix notes “With one grade shown there is nothing to compare yet.” Revealing later grades adds their cross-grade cells.
- **Thirty sites.** The card states 303 of 435 pairs, with risk .160 and expected share wrong .121. Adjacent-grade shares are .2019, .1672 and .0640.

```{=html}
<details>
<summary>Sorting within grades and marginal intervals</summary>
<p>Expected rank averages a unit's position under the posterior, with the top position first. Sorting by posterior mean can rearrange rows within a grade while keeping same-grade comparisons withheld and preserving the report's risk. These synthetic posteriors are taken as given; Grade 1 declares priority (highest synthetic need in the poverty example). Each interval describes one unit alone, and overlap does not determine grades. The larger example restricts its search to contiguous cuts of the expected-rank order from the poverty criterion of <code>pr_example_gaussian</code>; the card follows the package's report-card plot and the between-grade table follows Figure 10 and Section VI.B of Kline, Rose and Walters.</p>
</details>
```

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" title="In postrank"}
```r
library(postrank)
one <- postrank(pr_tutorial$one, tau=.2, G_max=3L, backend="highs", fragility=FALSE)
one$fit$evaluation[c("G", "N", "M", "disclosure_rate")]
```
:::
